heading: Why world No.1 Sinner cannot afford to skip the Asian swing despite his injury, especially after US Open withdrawal
author: Edited by: Soror Shaiza / TIMESOFINDIA.COM /  Sep 21, 2026, 20:47 IST
paragraphs: Jannik Sinner has not played a match since lifting the Wimbledon trophy on July 12, and his absence from the US Open has now turned the next few weeks into a careful balancing act
The world No. 1 can return in Asia, where he has already experienced problems in difficult conditions, or wait for the indoor season and build towards the ATP Finals in Turin

Either route carries a cost, with Alexander Zverev waiting for an opportunity.Sinner's comeback could be delayed until ViennaSinner's last appearance came at Wimbledon on July 12, when he won the title, and more than two months have now passed without another competitive match.The Italian was forced to withdraw from the 2026 US Open before the tournament because of a right knee issue, which had also kept him out of the preceding North American hard-court events in Montreal and Cincinnati

It was the first Grand Slam tournament Sinner had missed since making his Flushing Meadows debut in 2019.His eventual return therefore remains uncertain, and former ATP professional Stefano Pescosolido believes Sinner could choose to miss the Asian swing altogether rather than immediately expose himself to the heat and humidity of Beijing and Shanghai.“I think he's a little more careful from a physical standpoint
He wants to avoid relapses,” Pescosolido told Tuttosport.“The Slams are his main goal, and I imagine he wants to be at his best next year to try to win as many as possible

There are two options: Beijing and Shanghai, or starting with the indoor tournaments.”The concern is not simply the knee problem that forced Sinner out of the US Open.Sinner has a documented history of struggling physically in hot conditions, including at the Australian Open over the past two years and at European events, while his most dramatic episode came at the French Open this year.Sinner was leading Juan Manuel Cerundolo and was one game away from victory in their second-round match at Roland Garros when he suffered severe cramps and a complete loss of energy, leaving him unable to mount a meaningful response.That collapse came after Sinner had played all five Masters 1000 tournaments in the build-up to Paris, with the accumulated workload becoming part of the discussion around his physical condition.China has presented similar problems.At the Shanghai Masters last year, Sinner struggled with the humidity and eventually retired during his match against Tallon Griekspoor, despite that contest being played in a night session.Pescosolido therefore believes the indoor season could offer a more controlled route back.“Last year, at the ATP 1000 tournament in China, the conditions were difficult and he withdrew due to cramps,” Pescosolido said. “He could skip the Asian trip and return from Vienna, to be ready for the ATP Finals, in order to best plan for the following year.”That would put the Erste Bank Open in Vienna at the centre of Sinner's potential comeback.The ATP 500 indoor hard-court tournament is scheduled for October 26 to November 1, 2026, at Vienna's Wiener Stadthalle, and Sinner has a particularly strong connection with the event after winning the title in 2023 and 2025.Returning indoors would also remove the heat and humidity that have contributed to some of his recent physical difficulties, while giving him competitive matches before the season-ending championship in Turin.Skipping China could put Sinner's No. 1 ranking under pressureThe problem with protecting his body is that Sinner's ranking does not stop moving simply because he is not playing.He has already qualified for the 2026 Nitto ATP Finals, which will be held at the Inalpi Arena in Turin from November 15 to November 22, but the Italian will have to consider what happens to his ranking if he remains away from the Asian tournaments.Sinner is the defending champion in Beijing, meaning that if he chooses not to play there, he would lose 500 ranking points

That would reduce his advantage over Alexander Zverev, even if the German also decided to skip the tournament.Zverev has relatively few points to defend from last year's Asian swing and could therefore make up further ground by going deep in Shanghai, particularly given the form he has shown after winning two Grand Slam titles this year.The German also has points to defend later in the indoor season, having reached the Vienna final and the Paris Masters semi-finals last year, but a strong Asian swing would still give him an opportunity to close the gap before Sinner returns.That creates a difficult calculation for Sinner.Playing in Beijing and Shanghai would allow him to defend ranking points and prevent Zverev from gaining ground, but it would also mean returning from a knee problem in the same type of hot and humid conditions that have previously caused him physical difficulties.Waiting until Vienna would give him an indoor environment and more time to prepare, but it would leave Zverev with an extended opportunity to challenge his position at the top of the rankings.Turin is the target Sinner has to protectThe wider objective is the Nitto ATP Finals, where Sinner will defend his title in front of his home crowd.The tournament brings together the top eight singles players and top eight doubles teams at the end of the ATP season, with this year's edition scheduled for November 15-22 in Turin.Sinner's indoor record makes a return through Vienna particularly attractive if he decides that avoiding Asia is the better option

He has won 10 titles from 12 indoor finals, including his two Vienna championships, giving him a strong competitive base on which to rebuild his rhythm before Turin.The timing also allows Sinner to think beyond the final weeks of 2026.There is, however, a reason Sinner may find the decision difficult even beyond the rankings.He has won two titles in Beijing and one in Shanghai during his career, meaning the Asian swing has been a productive part of his schedule rather than an unwanted detour

Skipping both tournaments would therefore mean giving up opportunities to compete in places where he has already enjoyed significant success.For now, the choice is between returning sooner in conditions that have previously tested him physically or waiting for the indoor courts of Vienna, where he has already proved himself twice.Either way, Sinner's next tournament will carry more weight than a routine return from injury, because the world No. 1 is trying to protect both his body and his position at the top before the season reaches its final stretch in Turin.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates
